correctness.rationale: The equilibrium is positive and satisfies every balance. The actual four-by-four Neumann mode matrix gives the exact shifted quartic and the Routh-Hurwitz determinants (both symbolically checked). The unit first disk eigenvalue has a double spatial eigenspace; the exact determinant and third determinant produce 0<h<h_- and h_+<h<h_osc as the only stable ranges. All other nonzero disk modes have kappa>5/4, making a4 strictly positive; a derivative polynomial strictly positive for t>=2 proves their oscillatory thresholds exceed h_osc. High-frequency sectorial damping excludes a hidden accumulation. At the first two thresholds the critical spectral value is zero, while the third is an imaginary pair with positive nonzero frequency and transverse crossing. Nonlinear local stability and instability follow from semilinear parabolic linearization. Symbolic checker corroborates identities and numerical Bessel samples are not an infinite proof.

Turing-Hopf analyses for two-field or heterogeneous models are structurally distinct. Classical Routh-Hurwitz theory is explicitly acknowledged. value.rationale: Two competing chemical feedback loops cause an analytically exact stationary instability, a nonzero recovered stability window, and an oscillatory instability on further gain increase. The all-Neumann-mode result and open-parameter robustness are useful for distinguishing real pattern-forming and wave-forming failures and demonstrate nonmonotonic feedback effectiveness; they go beyond substituting numbers into a known table. Narrowness of the interval is explicitly reported and does not reduce the proof to an arbitrary threshold recomputation.
